coverage: Available authoritative reports, whitelisted aggregate artifacts and prior-session playback evidence; not a claim of raw reconstruction for every historical run.
cost_semantics: Provider-reported usage only; null means not consolidated, not zero. Calls retain the logical/provider-completion distinctions stated in each entry. No cross-entry cost total.

entries.title: Timing, provider failures and mock validation
entries.scope: 5,914-profile timing preparation; later Ohio mock: 226 profiles, 164 valid targets, 30 repetitions.
entries.result: Strict pre-cutoff and paper-faithful profiles were separated. A retrospective two-field baseline scored 0.076340 Brier. The mock produced 13,560 predictions; its 0.105333 individual and 0.116824 society Brier scores measure mechanics only. Credit, authentication and retired-model failures are retained in the status log.
entries.decision: Keep retrospective conditioning and mock checks separate from live human-response evidence.
entries.limitations: The retrospective baseline conditions on information after the strict cutoff. Failed requests do not establish completed experiments; no combined bill is inferred.

entries.title: Early live smoke excluded from protocol evidence
entries.scope: Completed smoke: four profiles, three scorable, 24 logical calls; earlier attempts incomplete.
entries.result: Brier 0.06547967 individual versus 0.088963 society was observed, but the OpenRouter path omitted the system instruction. Across three attempts: 72 request reservations, $0.00880242 reported, one unresolved reservation.
entries.decision: Retain receipts; exclude these scores from claims about the corrected protocol.
entries.limitations: Reservations, logical calls and provider attempts differ. Usage total covers overlapping attempts, not an additional independent run.

entries.title: Corrected individual versus society run
entries.scope: 24 unique people, 22 scorable, two repetitions; 48 reflections, 48 public messages, 48 ballots.
entries.result: Individual Brier 0.11673581; society 0.14847838. Replication differences had opposite signs. Earlier corrected attempts stopped after 98 logical completions and after a first-call format failure; they remain incomplete.
entries.decision: No reliable interaction advantage.

entries.title: Profile and evidence factorial
entries.scope: 24 new Ohio people, four individual conditions; 12-person social subset.
entries.result: Vote Brier: sparse 0.106901, sparse + evidence 0.134875, rich 0.089928, rich + evidence 0.103553. Social versus private: vote 0.108627/0.090723, healthcare 0.254590/0.291924, gun 0.365767/0.419940.
entries.decision: Mixed outcome-specific effects; do not promote context or interaction as generally beneficial.
entries.limitations: Narrow economic context is available evidence, not verified individual exposure; only 18 vote targets scorable.

entries.title: 120-person profile comparison
entries.scope: 120 inspected development people; three models; a separate 50-person reserve excluded.
entries.decision: No progression. The folder name “reserved-validation” does not make these now-inspected people untouched.
entries.limitations: 482 reservations included two unresolved read timeouts; reported cost is incomplete billing. Target counts 84/116/120 differ.

entries.title: Vote pilot and synthetic-population check
entries.scope: 16-person LLM pilot; 135 eligible statistical-evaluation records; separate 1,000-person synthetic population.
entries.result: Rich LLM Brier 0.13609 versus basic 0.30290; rich naive Bayes 0.01925 on the same 16 and 0.09927 on 135. Peer conditions did not beat rich individual prediction. Synthetic Democratic two-party share 51.8014% versus official 51.5146%, but predicted turnout exceeded the official count by about 1.39 million.
entries.decision: Close aggregate vote share is insufficient behavioral validation; preserve the turnout correction.
entries.limitations: Effective pilot sample about 10.8; self-reported turnout is not validated turnout. Statistical samples must be distinguished.

entries.title: Expanded three-outcome attitude comparison
entries.scope: 226 Ohio people; valid targets healthcare 221, gun 226, environment 225.
entries.result: Full multiclass Brier, basic/rich/logistic: healthcare 0.66999/0.55004/0.50910; gun 0.58653/0.56180/0.47719; environment 0.67847/0.61459/0.54280. Rich profiles improved point estimates; logistic remained best on all three. Rich-minus-basic intervals excluded zero for healthcare and environment, not gun policy.
entries.decision: Keep rich profiles as a development finding; retain logistic as the benchmark.
entries.limitations: Brier scale 0–2; bootstrap intervals are descriptive and conditional, not full complex-survey uncertainty.

entries.title: Separate calibration and transfer
entries.scope: 240 people outside Ohio/New Jersey: 160 fit, 80 validation; then frozen Ohio transfer.
entries.result: Validation raw → calibrated Brier: healthcare 0.52873 → 0.49867, gun 0.60027 → 0.53570, environment 0.72427 → 0.63460. Ohio: 0.55004 → 0.58293, 0.56180 → 0.52402, 0.61459 → 0.55935. Logistic still beat calibrated LLM forecasts on all three Ohio outcomes.
entries.decision: Calibration is outcome- and sample-dependent; it did not generally repair prediction.
entries.limitations: Only the validation environment interval excluded zero. The $0.3208856 reserved amount is not billed cost.

entries.title: Initial isolated interaction pilot
entries.scope: 32 people, eight groups, four topics; 14 changed and 18 unchanged answers.
entries.result: RPS: persistence 0.16250, private 0.15808, generated discussion 0.12166, real-message replay 0.11116. Discussion-minus-private -0.03642, interval [-0.07418, -0.00178]; versus persistence interval [-0.11170, 0.02350] crossed zero.
entries.decision: Motivated the larger comparison; not confirmation of society simulation.
entries.limitations: Small selected pilot. Real-message replay is a diagnostic with observed discussion information.

entries.title: Isolation and ANES software checks
entries.scope: Separate Ohio checkout and Docker development checks.
entries.result: Recorded suite: 253 passed plus 39 targeted tests; later fixes reached 290 then 294. Real 2012 ANES data were correctly rejected under the June 2012 cutoff because fieldwork/release occurred later. A 48-vote mock exercised two questions.
entries.decision: Use an explicit retrospective contract; passing tests do not establish human fidelity.
entries.limitations: Counts are stage-specific and overlapping; do not add them or describe them as a new full-suite run.

entries.title: Controlled peer follow-up
entries.scope: 40 profiles, three repetitions; 38 valid healthcare targets.
entries.result: Mean full Brier, reconsideration/grouped peer: healthcare 0.569933/0.536531, gun 0.546849/0.499083, environment 0.614939/0.659114. Grouped arithmetic beat grouped agents on healthcare and environment. Same-cohort logistic: 0.468742, 0.509153, 0.461641; peer agents had the lower gun-policy point estimate only.
entries.decision: Retain the narrow positive gun result and the negative outcomes together.
entries.limitations: 362 reservations; two HTTP 502 requests have unknown charges. Recovery preserved completed predictions. No significance claim or independent human replications; $0.6278636 is conservative reservation.

entries.title: Observed media and historical availability audit
entries.scope: 226 Ohio people; eight observed categorical media predictors; archive/source review.
entries.result: Rich → rich + measured-media logistic Brier: healthcare 0.509103 → 0.508760, gun 0.477193 → 0.495882, environment 0.542803 → 0.549810. The October 20 archived debate transcript was available before only 64 of 226 interview starts. Fifty-eight broadcast metadata records are not 58 independent stories.
entries.decision: No overall feature gain. Preserve interview cutoffs and reject heuristic outlet weights as measured audience evidence.
entries.limitations: Publication date is not proof of contemporaneous archival availability or personal exposure. POST discussion fields excluded; this is not causal media analysis.

entries.title: Reserve evaluator and cross-year candidates
entries.scope: New Jersey evaluator/access audit and cross-year questionnaire readiness.
entries.result: Existing reports document reserve controls and candidate item/mode comparisons. They do not establish an authorized new reserve readout or successful longitudinal transfer.
entries.decision: Keep later outcomes outside development. Use source-backed crosswalks before execution.
entries.limitations: This compilation did not open New Jersey targets, respondent exports or reserved evaluator outcomes.

entries.title: Focused profiles and private review
entries.scope: 24 previously inspected people, two repetitions, four arms; 96 other development people fit baselines; 50-person reserve excluded.
entries.result: Macro weighted half-multiclass Brier: prevalence 0.29645, party 0.25009, sparse 0.26736, rich 0.27166, focused 0.25996, focused + review 0.26601. Focused-minus-rich -0.01170, interval [-0.04104, 0.01600].
entries.decision: No demonstrated advantage over the party baseline or progression criterion.
entries.limitations: 192 final forecasts and 48 reviews; Brier uses half-multiclass normalization, unlike the separate Ohio report.

entries.title: Profile ablation and statistical hybrids
entries.scope: 120 inspected people, four arms, two repetitions; nested 5-outer/4-inner development folds.
entries.result: Direct macro Brier: sparse 0.23786, rich 0.23778, reduced 0.23871, reduced + observed 0.23184; party baseline 0.22087. Hybrid scores 0.22821/0.22235/0.22590/0.22483. Added observed information change -0.00686, interval [-0.01867, 0.00350].
entries.decision: No candidate promoted; keep the separate 50-person reserve untouched.
entries.limitations: Conditional intervals omit baseline refit uncertainty; this is development reuse, not fresh confirmation.

entries.title: Published enrollment estimates reproduced
entries.scope: 74,922 people, 66,385 households; two full-sample Table III enrollment rows.
entries.result: Lottery assignment increased ever-enrollment by 25.5866 percentage points (household-clustered SE 0.3509 points), and endpoint enrollment on September 30, 2009 by 14.8139 points (SE 0.3112). All six published-rounding checks passed. This reproduces enrollment findings, not the entire paper.
entries.decision: Retain as a verified historical statistical reference; no agent or health-outcome claim.
entries.limitations: Medicaid, not Medicare. Unit-weight OLS with lottery-draw and listed-household-size indicators; household CR1 standard errors. Raw control means and adjusted assignment coefficients are different estimands. Full-sample inspection leaves no pristine holdout inside this sample.

entries.title: Household out-of-fold enrollment prediction
entries.scope: Five household-separated folds; assignment and selected administrative/list features.
entries.result: Brier 0.16769607 assignment-only → 0.16421990 fixed-L2 logistic, an absolute reduction of 0.00347618 (2.07% relative). Log loss 0.51126394 → 0.50097743. No LLM calls.
entries.decision: Resolve the pre-event feature/cutoff contract before a matched agent comparison; keep the statistical model.
entries.limitations: No difference interval; age omitted, so not the strongest available statistical baseline. Matched lottery draw is analyst alignment, not personal information. No individual causal, health, current-system or prospective forecast validation.

entries.title: Larger six-arm comparison
entries.scope: 116 people, 29 evaluation groups/topics; 47 other groups and 188 people fit development baseline.
entries.result: RPS: direct 0.115118, transition 0.130286, real replay 0.131949, generated discussion 0.146711, reflection 0.149433, persistence 0.163793. Discussion-minus-baseline +0.01643, interval [-0.01698, 0.05190]; discussion-minus-direct +0.03159, interval [0.00791, 0.05933]. False modal changes: discussion 28/58 unchanged people, direct 17/58.
entries.decision: Retain direct prediction as a useful reference; do not expand interaction. These 29 groups are now exposed.
entries.limitations: One model/generation; direct-baseline lead is a point estimate without a prespecified contrast interval. Source drift in three files caused the original final check to fail; frozen-source recovery reconstructed saved calls without new provider jobs. Not a clean original integrity pass. Original raw run folder not materialized in this worktree.

entries.title: Participant admission and message dataset
entries.scope: 47 downloaded development groups; 33 admitted: 29 training and four validation.
entries.result: Fourteen groups excluded by receipt matching; 831 training and 133 validation messages prepared. Ninety-six unused candidate groups remain metadata-only, not admitted fresh evaluation.
entries.decision: Preserve participant/source overlap checks and separate admitted from merely discovered data.
entries.limitations: Documentation-level admission does not imply independently verified unique humans across all sessions.

entries.title: OpenRouter format smoke
entries.scope: 12 responses; 10 valid.
entries.result: Two outputs failed formatting. This was not a scientific evaluation.
entries.decision: Keep invalid-response costs and failures in the record.

entries.title: Single-group hosted development diagnostic
entries.scope: Four already-inspected people in one group.
entries.result: RPS: private 0.102925, transition 0.146322, persistence 0.200000, direct 0.204770, discussion 0.239250.
entries.decision: Do not use one group to overturn the larger comparison or rank models generally.
entries.limitations: No independent evaluation or intervals; baseline participant overlap was not audited for this diagnostic. Not a base-versus-SFT comparison.

entries.title: Laptop pilot and memory probes
entries.scope: Recorded laptop: MacBook Air M5, 24 GB memory, 10-core GPU; quantized Llama 3.1 8B.
entries.result: LoRA pilot: 52 microsteps/13 updates, batch 1 with accumulation 4, rank 8 over 16 layers; 223.99 seconds, about 40 MiB adapter. Eight-batch validation loss 5.024 → 3.457 was diagnostic. System swap rose about 2.8 → 6.3 GiB. Both subsequent memory probes completed (~70–71 seconds; about 6.52 GiB peak MLX allocation).
entries.decision: Small supervised runs fit the laptop, but resource feasibility does not establish predictive utility.
entries.limitations: System swap is shared by all applications. Hardware measurements describe these saved runs, not an unrestricted training capacity.

entries.title: Matched base/adapter comparison
entries.scope: 133 messages, four groups, 3,415 supervised tokens; matched prompt/source bindings.
entries.result: Token-weighted NLL 3.627999 → 3.201114; equal-group NLL 3.970071 → 3.304992. All four groups improved message likelihood. Direct belief format: base 16/16 valid; adapter first output invalid (822 non-JSON characters), so stopped after 1/16.
entries.decision: Message imitation improved, but belief-outcome superiority was not evaluated.
entries.limitations: Validation had already supplied eight training-time diagnostic batches; it is not untouched confirmation. No outcome scoring after format failure.

entries.title: Bounded format diagnosis
entries.scope: Four training people × two models × two prompt styles = 16 generations.
entries.result: Base original 4/4 valid; base prefix 3/4 (one vector summed to 0.99). Adapter 0/4 for both styles; all prefixed vectors were zero. Run completed in 50.79 seconds.
entries.decision: A prompt prefix did not rescue the adapter; avoid a larger outcome run.
entries.limitations: No outcome evaluation. Independent reviewer hit a spending cap; final root review must not be labeled independent.

entries.title: Task-aligned classifier pilot
entries.scope: 92 fit people/23 groups; 24 internal people/six groups; 52 microsteps/13 updates.
entries.result: RPS base 0.184574, candidate 0.216049, persistence 0.133333, transition 0.124716. Candidate-minus-base +0.031475 exceeded the +0.02 nonworsening limit. Change-event Brier improved 0.397598 → 0.379312, but expected-category MAE worsened 1.332604 → 1.511860.
entries.decision: Stop this candidate; secondary improvement does not override the primary failed gate.
entries.limitations: Native offline training 43.78 seconds, peak 5.10 GiB. Six-label probability mass fell 0.984780 → 0.654332; this is not a calibration score.

entries.title: Training, error and method audit
entries.scope: Saved classifier outputs and admitted fit cohort; no new training.
entries.result: No implementation bug identified. The candidate chose category 4 for 23/24 people; 14 unchanged people accounted for 88.6% of the gap to the transition baseline. Reconstructed training exposure covered 52/92 people and 21/23 groups. A 52-case statistical control scored 0.134724 versus 0.124716 for all 92, still far better than candidate 0.216049.
entries.decision: Investigate target/data design; the evidence does not justify asserting that more training will fix the failure.
entries.limitations: Exposure was reconstructed, not observed in a training log. Leave-one-group sensitivity is descriptive, not a new independent test.

entries.title: Frozen-model residual calibration
entries.scope: 92 fit people, 23 groups, 21 topic/person components; five folds of 20/20/20/16/16.
entries.result: Equal-group normalized RPS: raw transition 0.141335935, calibrated control 0.140185794, control + frozen logits 0.140233300. Gain over raw 0.001102635 was below 0.01; extension was worse than control by 0.000047505. Ten bounded fits converged; model coefficient effectively zero in four folds.
entries.decision: Keep the statistical baseline; stop before refit/internal/outer stages.
entries.limitations: Independent audit reproduced probabilities exactly and metrics within 1e-12. Ninety-two base forwards took 32.56 seconds, peak 4.59 GiB, no observed swap growth. No new neural training or internal/outer outcome read.

entries.title: Statistical reference frozen and data audited
entries.scope: 92 admitted people, 23 groups, 21 topics; 48 unchanged, 44 changed.
entries.result: Required fields were present and valid; initial-category counts ranged from 10 to 22. The exact six-category Laplace-one transition table was retained, not replaced by a calibrated variant. SHA-256 ffc4ecc705c209841dfe51bcab5b40f68159c91cb914ef4e362c4abdda46b245.
entries.decision: Improve data and design before further model training.
entries.limitations: Completeness of the admitted export does not establish selection representativeness or adequate sample size.

entries.title: Linked-panel source and design readiness
entries.scope: Proposed seven-category party ID: 2016 → 2020 development; separately frozen 2020 → 2024 later evaluation.
entries.result: Development auditor, reference functions and readiness gates implemented; 52 relevant tests reported. Five source blockers remain: 2024 summary construction, unavailable original documentation bytes, unverified repeated-variable archive, release/errata alignment, and unverified merged schema/linkage/missing codes. No respondent dataset ingested.
entries.decision: Archive source documentation, resolve equivalence and freeze a development-only projection before ingestion; then fit a new seven-category baseline.
entries.limitations: Derived paraphrase hash is not an original-source hash. One early transition cannot test a matched long-history ablation. Candidate, practical margin and design-aware uncertainty remain unresolved; later evaluation and model training disabled.

entries.title: Research playback and aggregate display
entries.scope: Available DEBATE recording selected; 51 recorded actions reported in the prior preview check.
entries.result: Playback operates on a materialized recording. “No actions” on an unavailable ANES run did not imply that a live job was running. Dashboard checks subsequently covered failed classifier/calibration gates and panel readiness as separate states.
entries.decision: Display recording availability, experiment status and live execution separately.
entries.limitations: The 51-action browser check is prior-session evidence, not a fresh October 27 browser check. Current server liveness was not tested in this compilation.

entries.title: Mock-mode provenance and routine offline verification
entries.scope: Separate automation/daily-swarm checkout; October 23 provenance fix and October 27 verification.
entries.result: Mock/live mode now participates in resumable-run provenance. Seven regression cases were added; 313 tests passed on October 23 and again October 27 with two existing warnings. Bounded mocks ran two questions × 12 votes, Brier 0.25.
entries.decision: Keep maintenance evidence separate from scientific outcomes; these checks do not refresh research-branch results.
entries.limitations: Research branch remained unmerged. Mock scores show mechanics, not model performance; October 27 checks did not test Docker isolation.
